## What doing it consciously looks like

Some of these lessons came through thought. Most arrived through failure. A few I’m still testing.

If I had to put the practical part on one card:

- Talk before making love: jealousy, attraction to other people, stress behavior, old patterns, how recent the healing is, what you want in a hard moment, money. Use real scenarios. If the answer stays abstract, I assume there probably isn’t an answer yet.
- Don’t let sex, moving in, and choosing a life partner turn into one yes. Housing can make separate living difficult. If you do move in, set a check-in date before there’s a crisis.
- Make friends together. Old friends are partial. Fine; make sure they aren’t the only people who know the relationship.
- A wonderful lover can still be a terrible co-parent, community member, or life partner. Catch “I’m taking a chance on this person” before it quietly becomes “this is the right person.”
- Keep your inner practices. Don’t let being loved become the reason you stop them.
- Don’t binge deep conversations. Leave room for play and ordinary life. Some things are better observed than extracted.
- If something says wait, slow down, or ask this, don’t let chemistry overrule it.

## What doing it consciously looks like

Most of these lessons came from me getting things wrong. Some came from thinking, and a few I’m still testing.

The short version for myself is: talk before making love about jealousy, other attractions, stress, old patterns, recent healing, hard moments, and money. Use an actual scenario. If the answer is only abstract, I assume there probably isn’t a real answer yet.

Don’t let sex answer the moving-in question, or moving in answer the life-partner question. Housing can make separate living difficult. If you do move in, put a check-in date on the calendar before there’s a crisis. A wonderful lover can still be a terrible co-parent, community member, or life partner. “I’m taking a chance on this person” is not “this is the right person.”

Make friends together. Old friends are partial; that’s fine. Just don’t let them be the only people who know the relationship.

Keep your inner practices. Don’t cram ten profound conversations into a weekend and call it depth either. Go do ordinary things. Some stuff is better observed than extracted. And when something in you says wait, slow down, ask this, don’t let chemistry make the call for you.
